title: Class enumeration in mixture models
text: bootstrap likelihood ratio test (McLachlan, 1987) compares two candidates differ one class. Data sets simulated smaller candidate candidates re-estimated . B simulated data sets, b yield likelihood ratio least large observed one, p-value (b + 1) / (B + 1) (Davison Hinkley, 1997); additional count includes observed statistic precludes p-value zero finite simulation. p-value withheld unless every replicate satisfies estimation checks. test compares three four profiles three group classes. Nineteen simulated data sets keep example brief; smallest attainable p-value 1/20 = 0.05, applied analyses use least 99.

title: Evaluating a multilevel latent profile model
text: course_engagement one row per course enrolment: 1,422 enrolments 106 students. student identifies group, five activity measures (browse, lectures, forum_read, forum_post, attendance) indicators, standardized within course.
code: library(latents)

title: Evaluating a multilevel latent profile model
text: fit model, call multilpa() vars indicators, id group, n_profiles number profiles, n_group_classes number group classes, n_starts number random EM starts, seed reproducible starts.
code: fit <- multilpa(course_engagement,                 vars = c("browse", "lectures", "forum_read", "forum_post",                          "attendance"),                 id = "student", n_profiles = 2, n_group_classes = 2,                 n_starts = 3, seed = 1)

title: Evaluating a multilevel latent profile model
text: check convergence, call get_results() "model". converged reports convergence best start, boundary whether variance reached lower bound, n_best_replicated many starts reached best log likelihood. variance lower bound profile one observation degenerate solution; fitting boundary = "exclude" keeps best start without one. profile fewer effective members means variances raises latents_thin_profiles warning: variances poorly determined, inspect covariance diagnostics interpreting . check individual starts, call get_results() "starts". check whether random seeds reach solution, call sensitivity() seeds seeds try. optimum numbers distinct maxima found, agreement share observations assigned original fit, matching arbitrary profile labels.

what: Estimate regression relationships that vary across latent classes — mixture_regression
title: Estimate regression relationships that vary across latent classes — mixture_regression
text: mixture_regression() examines whether relationship outcome predictors differs across latent classes. represents conditional outcome distribution mixture class-specific regression models, allowing classes differ outcome levels, predictor associations, trajectories time. Regression parameters class-membership probabilities estimated jointly maximum likelihood. Coefficients may vary across classes , selected predictor terms, constrained common value. Predictors outcome formula describe variation within classes; covariates supplied membership describe variation probability belonging class. Posterior membership probabilities express uncertainty assigning observations groups estimated classes. function supports Gaussian, binomial, Poisson, negative-binomial, ordinal outcome models, subject restrictions described . Class membership may defined individual observations shared across repeated observations unit. time predictors, shared membership defines class-specific trajectories; Gaussian random effects additionally allow individual trajectories vary within classes.

title: Estimate regression relationships that vary across latent classes — mixture_regression
text: repeated measurements (id, class_level = "group"), including time formula specifies class-specific trajectories. Without random effects, latent class growth model (Nagin, 2005). Argument random adds within-class variation individual trajectories, yielding growth mixture model (Verbeke Lesaffre, 1996; Muthen Shedden, 1999). individual class k, model $$y_i = X_i \beta_k + Z_i b_i + e_i, \quad b_i \sim N(0, G_k), \quad e_i \sim N(0, \sigma_k^2 ),$$ Z design matrix specified random. Gaussian random effects integrated analytically. Estimation uses EM followed quasi-Newton optimization analytic scores. fitted object class latents_growth_mixture; tables plots described get_results() plot(). Random effects require gaussian family, id class_level = "group". residual_correlation, residuals also carry process shared classes, \(e_i \sim N(0, W_i + \sigma_k^2 )\): continuous-time autoregressive process ("ar") Brownian motion ("brownian") residual_time, corresponding correlation structures specified lcmm::hlme(cor = ). cluster, persons nested clusters (students schools) multilevel growth mixture model fitted: cluster belongs group class h, trajectory-class logits persons group-class-specific intercept shared covariate slopes, $$L = \prod_j \sum_h \omega_h \prod_{\j} \sum_k \pi_{k|h} f_k(y_i)$$ (Asparouhov Muthen 2008; Vermunt 2003). group_membership names cluster-level covariates group class. group classes returned get_results(fit, "group_classes") "clusters".

what: Fit a two-level latent profile model — multilpa
title: Fit a two-level latent profile model — multilpa
text: Multilevel latent profile analysis describes heterogeneity among observations among groups nested. Examples include repeated measurements within individuals students within schools. Observation-level profiles describe patterns indicators, group-level classes describe differences probabilities profiles. standard model, profile definitions shared across group classes: given profile indicator means covariance structure every group class. Group classes therefore differ profile composition. Observations within group can belong different profiles, membership probabilities depending group's latent class. multilpa() estimates measurement parameters, conditional profile probabilities, group-class proportions, posterior membership probabilities levels. default specification uses Gaussian indicators diagonal within-profile covariance matrices. Alternative specifications support covariance structures, discrete mixed indicators, predictors latent membership.
